messages:
maya: infra-bot fired an alert for repeated KV-cache OOMs on prod-rt-7. multiple pods hit OOM within 5m for long-context jobs.
infra-bot: [ALERT] kv_cache_memory_exhausted on prod-rt-7 (3 instances) — traces attached.
maya: summary from initial triage: spike correlates with yesterday's runtime v1.23 rollout + new batching heuristic. looks like KV allocation grows superlinearly for sequences > 8k.
ryan: saw same on a repro run locally. when we use the newer attention kernel it allocs a temp KV buffer that isn't freed until end-of-request. increases peak by ~25%. pprof snippet: `heap  top  -  120MB    35% // kv slab`
zhen: also observed that the batching merge logic now aggregates by token budget instead of request count; that made a few long requests be batched together into a single larger KV working set.
elaine: can we confirm it's kernel selection + batching interacting, not a pure leak?
ryan: yes — pmap shows no leak across requests in long-run test. memory returns to baseline between jobs when we force the old kernel. timeline: v1.23 switched to kernel 'attn-dense-v2' for small heads which uses a transient per-layer KV scratch.
maya: good. immediate mitigation options? short list: 1) revert kernel selection for longctx paths, 2) tighten batching to cap cumulative seq_len per batch, 3) enable KV on-alloc eviction spill, 4) soft reject/shorten extremely long requests.
zhen: i pushed a quick flag we can flip: `runtimectl feature set attn.kernel.selector=legacy --env=prod-rt-7` — flips kernel routing for models with >4096 seq. recommends canary first.
ryan: also created a runtime flag for aggressive kv eviction: `runtimectl set kv.eviction_mode=aggressive --grace=100ms` this will evict cold KV entries during allocation to avoid OOM. downside: possible perf regressions for very long-turn dialogs.
elaine: for telemetry/alerts we should add a short-window alert on eviction rate + p99 latency to detect regressions. i'll add an alert: `kv.evictions > 50/s && latency.p99 > 1.2x baseline`
maya: proposal for immediate roll: 1) flip kernel selector on two canary nodes, 2) enable kv.eviction_mode=aggressive on canaries, 3) run a canary load with long-context synthetic traces (8k-16k tokens) for 30m, 4) if stable, rollout to the rest. owners: ryan + zhen own the canary, elaine owns alerts.
ryan: running canary now. command: `deployctl roll --cluster prod-rt-7 --canary 2 --image runtime:v1.23-rollback-kernel`
zhen: while canary runs, i'm going to run a profiler that dumps slab fragmentation and kvcache pages: `pprof --url http://canary/pdebug/heap -> kv_slab.txt` and `kv-pager stats` for eviction hits.
maya: research note — a longer-term fix is to change the batching heuristic to cap merged-batch by token variance: i.e., do not merge two requests if combined token count > max_tokens_per_batch (not just count-based). reduces tail growth.
ryan: agree. also looking at a fallback path: if allocation fails we should try a graceful degrade: 1) retry single-request with kernel=legacy and kv_eviction=aggressive, 2) if still fails, return a 503 with hint to client about shortening context, or 3) fall back to compact model variant that stores only every-other layer KV for huge contexts.
elaine: can we avoid returning 503s for user-facing chats? prefer short partial responses + background retry. but for API customers 503 with a structured error is ok.
zhen: implemented a retry loop in the allocator: `try_alloc -> on OOM -> trigger_kv_eviction(true) -> downgrade_kernel -> retry(1)` tested locally, reduced OOM rate by ~70% in synthetic. pushing a PR for review.
maya: ok timeline: - canary flip (ryan) now - allocator retry PR (zhen) review + merge within 2h - alert updates (elaine) in parallel - batching heuristic change scoped and scheduled for next sprint.
ryan: canary looks good so far (10m in). no OOMs, p99 latency +6% but within SLA. I'll hold on full rollout until zhen's allocator change lands.
elaine: alert thresholds updated and temporary incident channel created. tagging on-call.
maya: postmortem action items: 1) kernel selection tests for longctx in CI, 2) token-aware batching regression tests, 3) KV eviction telemetry + dashboards, 4) graceful degrade playbook (retry+downgrade). assigning: ryan(1), zhen(2+4), elaine(3).
ryan: noted. i'll start the full rollout once allocator retry is merged and canary runs 1h with stable metrics.
zhen: PR is merged to canary a few minutes ago, running validation. initial results show 0 OOMs across 30m load and eviction count rose but within expected.
maya: thanks all — i'll close this thread after the full rollout. please post any anomalies in this thread. :thumbsup:
__notes: autogenerated slack thread on kv cache OOM investigation
